From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
kayak
Wikipedia

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • kaiak, kiack, kyack, kyak, qayaq, kayack, qajaq

Etymology

[edit]

    Borrowed from Inuktitut ᖃᔭᖅ (qayaq, “hunter's boat”) (Inuvialuktun), from Proto-Eskimo *qayaʁ. Compare Greenlandic qajaq and Yup'ik qayaq.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (UK, US) IPA(key): /ˈkaɪˌæk/
    • Audio (Southern England):(file)
    • Audio (US):(file)
    • Rhymes: -aɪæk

    Noun

    [edit]

    kayak (plural kayaks)

    1. A type of small boat, covered over by a surface deck, powered by the occupant or occupants using a double-bladed paddle in a sitting position, from a hole in the surface deck.
      • 2018 July 17, Autumn Spanne, “Check out these crazy rock formations across the United States”, in CNN‎[1]:
        It’s just offshore from private property inaccessible to the general public, so a good way to approach the rock is by kayak, which can be rented in the small village of Port Austin.

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • kayak cross
    • kayak polo
    • kayak roll
    • kayak slalom
    • kayak sprint
    • kayaktivism
    • kayaktivist

    • → Khmer: កាយ៉ាក់ (kaayak)
    • → Korean: 카약 (kayak)
    • → Portuguese: caiaque

    Verb

    [edit]

    kayak (third-person singular simple present kayaks, present participle kayaking, simple past and past participle kayaked)

    1. (intransitive) To use a kayak, to travel or race in a kayak.
      Kayaking is an Olympic sport.
    2. (transitive) To traverse (a body of water) by kayak.
      On a dare, he kayaked the Harlem River in New York from Hell's Gate to Spyten Duyvil.

    Indonesian

    [edit]

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    From Betawi kaya', kaya, from Javanese ꦏꦪ (kaya, “like, such as”), from Old Javanese kaya (“like, as, as if, it looks as if”), from Pali काय (kāya), from Sanskrit क (ka, “similarity (suffix)”).

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • kaya
    • kek
    • kyk

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): [ˈka.jaʔ]
    • Hyphenation: ka‧yak

    Preposition

    [edit]

    kayak

    1. (colloquial) like, such as
      Synonyms: bagaikan, macam, sebagai, seperti

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    From Dutch kajak, from English kayak, from Inuktitut ᖃᔭᖅ (qayaq, “man's boat”), from Proto-Eskimo *qayaʁ.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): [ˈka.jak]
    • Hyphenation: ka‧yak

    Noun

    [edit]

    kayak (plural kayak-kayak)

    1. (sports) kayak
      Synonym: sampan
